source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:3 (the Hilleli; all precise books; Or Torah — against the printed Masorah's 'both defective')
claim_en: THE DREAM FILLS, THEN LEANS: God comes to Avimelech בחלום ('in a DREAM,' 20:3) — the FIRST dream-word PLENE with vav; and Minchat Shai's own pun stands against the printers who wrote 'both defective': they 'were as dreamers.' SNAPSHOT: the vav stands at the first.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:3 (the same ruling's second half)
claim_en: ...and the SECOND dream-word (בחלם, 20:6 — where God answers inside the dream) is DEFECTIVE, exactly as the Hilleli and the precise books rule: full at the arrival, lean at the answer.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 20:11; Minchat Shai (the Masorah's one-plene-one-defective pair)
claim_en: והרגוני ('and they will KILL ME for my wife') — ONE Torah token (20:11), written PLENE; the Masorah's defective twin is Jeroboam's 'they will kill me and return to Rehoboam' (I Kings 12:27; edge) — the Kitzur's spelling-moral: Gerar's men plene, 'for they were not as wicked as the idolaters.' The fear-formula's fullness grades the feared.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:2 (the Ramah: 'one word, and all the Torah likewise')
claim_en: Avimelech — written as ONE WORD at every occurrence: SNAPSHOT, whole-Torah census: twenty-one single word-rows, none split. The king's name never divides.

source: Masekhet Soferim (the dispute); R. Chananiah; Onkelos; Bereshit Rabbah's three-fold holy reading; Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Ralbag (via Minchat Shai on 20:13)
claim_en: THE DISPUTED NAME ON A PLURAL VERB: התעו אתי אלהים ('when God/the powers CAUSED ME TO WANDER' — the verb is PLURAL, DB-morph 3cp): Soferim records the dispute — some rule the Name PROFANE (the plural read of the wandering), R. Chananiah rules HOLY, Onkelos renders holy, Bereshit Rabbah expounds it holy three ways. SNAPSHOT: the plural form letter-exact — the grammatical fact both camps argue from. Holy/profane layer, station five: disputed.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:6 (the Masorah's seventeen; the Ramah's nine masculine)
claim_en: אותך ('YOU' — 'I withheld YOU from sinning') — PLENE with vav: one of the Masorah's plene object-pronouns (the Ramah counts nine masculine). SNAPSHOT: full, in the verse where God credits the withholding.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:6 (with Shaarei Orah and the Zohar's needle-reading)
claim_en: מחטו לי ('from SINNING against Me') — written WITHOUT the aleph: the sin-word lean by a letter; the mystics read the missing aleph into needles (מחטים) pressed into Avimelech's angel (Shaarei Orah; named). SNAPSHOT: no aleph.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 20:5 (all books; his Bereshit ruling)
claim_en: הלא ('did he not himself say...') — DEFECTIVE (no vav), not among the Torah's plene questions (a manuscript Masorah's addition declined); and WITHOUT maqqef. SNAPSHOT: lean and unjoined, both as ruled.
...the no-maqqef half of the ruling, machine-checked: the question-word stands free.

ולשרה ('and to Sarah...') — exactly TWICE in the Torah, and the pair preaches: 'and to Sarah he SAID: behold, a COVERING OF EYES' (20:16) with 'and to Sarah — A SON' (18:14): the Kitzur reads the covering of eyes forward into that son's own dimming eyes (27:1, named). The two Sarah-datives: the shielding and the promise.

ויתפלל ('and he shall PRAY for you' — spoken of the corpus's FIRST prophet-titled man): the prayer-word's whole Torah career is FOUR tokens, and it OPENS in this chapter twice (the promise 20:7, the performance 20:17) before Moses' two (Num 11:2, 21:7); the Masorah's three-list adds the idolater who 'bows and prays' (Isa 44:17) and the ever-needed prayer (Ps 72:15; edges) — 'not that hour alone: always he needed his prayer' (Kitzur).

מה עשית ('WHAT HAVE YOU DONE to us') — 'without pashta': the question-word's verb carries mahpakh (the turning accent), not the postpositive stroke. SNAPSHOT exact — the garden's question-form (the machine's mah-asita roster: God twice, then three kings) reaches Gerar pointed as ruled.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 52:5; Bereshit Rabbah 74:7; Onkelos Genesis 20:3
claim_en: A GRADE OF PROPHECY IS ASSIGNED AT THIS VERSE, AND BOTH SPINE MEMBERS CARRY IT INDEPENDENTLY. Bereshit Rabbah states the machine: the prophets of the nations receive at NIGHT, by half-speech, from behind a curtain, as one speaks to a concubine - with this king enrolled in the census beside Balaam and Laban - where Israel's prophets receive in full and direct speech. Onkelos carries the SAME grade distinction by a different device: the revelation to this king is routed through the WORD, 'the Word from before the LORD came to Avimelech', where Abraham's revelations in these units come direct. The chain says it and the translation encodes it, neither citing the other.

check.note: A prophecy-grade distinction stated by one spine member and independently encoded by the other through its reverence buffer - convergence without citation.

claim_en: THE SECOND LEG OF THE NO-FOREWARNING RULE STANDS IN THIS BLOCK. From our 20:7's 'know that you shall surely die' - said without any prior warning having been given - the chain takes a second derivation that the descendants of Noah are liable without forewarning. Both legs of that law are seated inside this parashah's own spans. The same verse is read as answering two questions at once: who will placate him - HE IS A PROPHET; and who will tell the world - he will PRAY for you.

check.note: The second of two derivations of one Noahide procedural rule, both seated in this parashah.

claim_en: OUR 20:6 IS READ AS DIVINE PREVENTION, NOT HUMAN RESTRAINT. 'I also withheld you from sinning against Me' is read with the phrase turned - your inclination is MINE - and argued by the horse-and-rider parable: the restraint was Mine, so the praise is Mine. The machine's withheld-sin operator is given an explicit agency reading that removes the credit from its subject.

check.note: A withheld-action operator assigned its agency explicitly, removing moral credit from the narrative's subject.

claim_en: THE NOTORIOUS PLURAL VERB OF OUR 20:13 IS RE-SUBJECTED IN TRANSLATION. The received ink reads a plural verb governed by the divine name - the crux of the verse - and Onkelos rewrites the clause entirely: 'when the NATIONS STRAYED after the works of their hands, God brought me NEAR to His fear from my father's house'. The plural is reassigned from God to the nations and the wandering becomes their straying, so the translation resolves a grammatical difficulty by changing who acts. A translation-layer decision on a standing crux, carried dual-track against the received text.

check.note: A plural verb governed by the divine name reassigned to a different subject in translation, resolving a grammatical crux by changing the actor.

claim_en: THE CLOSING TRANSACTION IS READ AS COMPENSATION, AND THE INDICTMENT IS READ AS RECIPROCAL. The chain maps the exchange of accusations onto the earlier verses, reading the offence-word as meaning PUNISHMENT and taking the womb-closure of our 20:18 back into the charge at 20:9. Onkelos reads the thousand pieces as a GARMENT OF HONOUR given in return for the taking, and the vindication clause as a granted right to reprove. The verse the machine records as an obscure payment is read by the translation as a stated compensation with a legal consequence.

check.note: An obscure transaction read as compensation with a granted right attached, and an accusation exchange mapped reciprocally onto earlier verses.

claim_en: THE FORGIVENESS LAW IS READ OFF THIS UNIT'S TWO EVENTS. Though the injurer pays, he is NOT FORGIVEN until he asks forgiveness of the injured - proof: 'now RESTORE the man's wife, for he is a prophet and will pray for you' (our 20:7, restoration alone insufficient). And the injured must not be cruel in withholding it - proof: 'and Abraham PRAYED to God, and God healed Abimelech' (our 20:17, the wronged interceding for his own wronger). Both events held as operator prose since derivation; the LAW made claim-visible through the Genesis sweep (finding F-008, owner: 'Yes update').

check.note: Case-shelf law; both proof texts are this unit's own verses, quoted by the Mishnah itself.

claim_en: THE DEFENSE EXHIBIT PRESSED AS STATUTE EVIDENCE AND DEFLECTED. The Noahide-relations sugya quotes our 20:12 to prove the MATERNAL sister banned to the sons of Noach (בת־אבי... אך לא בת־אמי — the father's-side permission proving the mother's side forbidden), and the gemara DEFLECTS the proof: she was his BROTHER'S daughter — kinship degree, not sister-law. The ban stands on the baraita; this verse's recorded role is attempted-and-deflected evidence. Seated from the Noahide exam (finding F-016; ruled seat under the owner's blanket word).

check.note: A verse's recorded evidentiary role (attempted proof, deflected) carried as a kept record, not as the law's source.
